name: Froonty
description:
A compact Dynamic-Island-style entry point at the top center of the screen that reuses GNOME Shell's own clock, calendar and notification facilities.

Clipboard access: with the Clipboard tab turned on in its settings (it is off by default), Froonty reads the clipboard on every copy and keeps a history of copied text, images and file locations on this computer only, so an entry can be copied again with a click. Passwords are never saved: copies marked secret by password managers, copies made in password managers and authenticators, and copied text that looks like a password are only listed hidden, in memory, for a few minutes (adjustable, or not at all). Nothing is sent anywhere, and there is no shortcut for clipboard data.
